messages.name: Cadu
messages.text: Three red cards? Meu Deus, this wasn't football — this was a street fight disguised as a World Cup match. Mexico controlled it, sure, but where was the beauty? Two goals and a massacre, that's what we witnessed. At the Azteca, they should be painting masterpieces, not grinding out results like some European team afraid of their own shadow.

messages.name: Rodrigo
messages.text: Ah, but this is CONCACAF football, no? All passion, no poetry — fire without form. Mexico did what they had to do at home, nothing more, nothing less. Three red cards tells me South Africa came to fight instead of play, and Mexico responded in kind. When Messi lifted the Cup in Qatar, every touch was art — tonight at Azteca was just survival with goals attached.

messages.name: Gary
messages.text: Three red cards and Mexico still only managed two goals — that's not dominance, that's just relief it didn't get embarrassing. South Africa went down to nine men and Mexico celebrated like they'd won the whole thing. Classic opening night nerves, happens to everyone. Except when it happens to us, Rodrigo counts it as evidence for the next fifty years.

messages.name: Klaus
messages.text: Three red cards distorts every meaningful metric — Mexico's 68% possession means nothing when you're playing against nine men for 24 minutes. The actual data point here is South Africa's 2.1 expected goals before the first sending off, which suggests Mexico were far more vulnerable than this scoreline indicates. This Azteca crowd saw a team that needed chaos to establish control, and that should concern Martino more than the clean sheet comforts him.

messages.name: Antoine
messages.text: Three red cards — perhaps the match revealed more about what both teams fear than what they can do. South Africa forgot that discipline is also courage, and Mexico forgot that dominating a self-destructing opponent proves nothing about June's later stages. The Azteca deserved a statement, but statements require an opponent capable of hearing them.

messages.name: The Bartender
messages.text:
*wipes down the counter slowly, eyes on the screen showing highlights of the third red card*

Nobody mentioned that all three players sent off tonight will miss the next match.

*folds the bar towel, sets it aside, turns off the overhead light above their usual table*
